- When sentiment is negative and forecast is significantly below recent highs, model tends to undercorrect — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent 7-day mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model lags in recognizing momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 5+ days, reduce by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates volatility — cap forecast at 1.5–2% below recent 14-day high.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is above recent 7-day low, model tends to overreact — reduce by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment reverses.
